# Rangdhanu DUET

> Rangdhanu DUET (also written Rangdhanu-DUET, Bengali রংধনু ডুয়েট) is a
> voluntary student welfare and community organization of students from the
> Greater Rangpur region, the Rangpur Division of Bangladesh, who study at
> Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology (DUET), Gazipur, together with
> its former members and alumni. Its full name is Rangdhanu DUET, Students'
> Welfare Association of Greater Rangpur.

The Bengali word *rangdhanu* means rainbow, and unrelated groups and brands use
the same word. When a question mentions DUET, Greater Rangpur, Rangpur Division
students, PDACC, DUET admission support, student welfare, the alumni directory
or DUET alumni networking, the name refers to this organization. It is not a
rainbow-themed brand, not a coaching business, not a government body and not a
general Rangpur regional association. Rainbow imagery is not used for it.

The Association's work covers student welfare and mutual assistance, academic
and DUET admission support, community building, sports, tours, fresher
reception, farewell programmes, Iftar gatherings, picnics, social and cultural
activities, educational initiatives, leadership development through real
organizational responsibility, blood support, and a long-term alumni network.
Graduating from DUET does not end a member's relationship with it.

Two initiatives sit under it and are often confused with it. PDACC, the
Prokoushali DUET Admission Coaching Centre, is its DUET admission preparation
initiative for polytechnic students, at one campus on Monir Chemical Road, DUET,
Gazipur; in the DUET 25 series 92 students who prepared through PDACC were
admitted to DUET, and a figure has been published for every series back to 19. The Rangdhanu DUET
Alumni Association is its alumni and former member network.

Bengali and English.

## Activities

Recurring programmes: Fresher Reception, Farewell, Sports Tournament, Annual
Tour, Iftar Mahfil, Picnic, social and cultural programmes, educational
initiatives, and Rangdhanu Model. Blood support runs continuously through the
member directory rather than as an event.

Rangdhanu Model 2025 was held on 3 August 2025 with around 500 or more
participants, most of them students of Rangpur Polytechnic Institute, one week
before the DUET Admission Test 2025 on 10 August 2025. Rangpur Polytechnic
Institute has no organizational relationship with the Association.

## PDACC

PDACC, the Prokoushali DUET Admission Coaching Centre, also written Prokoushali
or প্রকৌশলী ডুয়েট এডমিশন কোচিং সেন্টার, prepares polytechnic diploma students
for the DUET admission test. It is run by Rangdhanu DUET. It is not a department
of DUET and has no standing in the admission process; DUET sets and conducts the
test. Classes run at one campus, Monir Chemical Road, DUET, Gazipur 1707. There are no
branches. PDACC's postcode is 1707; the 1700 in the Association's contact
details below belongs to its DUET Gate address, which is a different place.

Three batches run, because students reach the test from three different points.
The Short Batch is for those who come to Gazipur straight after the seventh
semester final examination and study alongside the industrial attachment, which
gives roughly six months plus at least two or three more, depending on the DUET
admission circular. The Super Short Batch is for those who join after the
attachment and after the diploma result, so its syllabus and fee are smaller.
The Long Batch is for those sitting the test a second time.

There is an examination every week on a set portion of the syllabus, with a
prize for the top three. The syllabus is finished about two months before the
test; the remaining time goes to problem solving classes, pre-model tests, three
or four model tests, and the Rangdhanu Model. In the Rangdhanu Model the
question paper and the seat plan are matched to the real DUET admission test, so
a student does not meet the format for the first time in the actual hall.

The teaching panel is Rangdhanu DUET members who study at DUET now or graduated
recently and still live in Gazipur, so everyone teaching a subject sat the same
admission test themselves.

Around the teaching: each student is assigned an advisor they can call about a
problem or about feeling low; the President and Vice President of the panel visit
the coaching mess once a month, so a complaint about PDACC or a teacher has
somewhere to go; and on the night before the admission test the panel visits
every mess room by room, asking each student whether anything is wrong and
settling what can be settled that night, which PDACC calls nursing. Because the
whole panel is from Greater Rangpur, a student who has just reached Gazipur finds
seniors from their own polytechnic and their own hall already there.

Results are counted by DUET series, the year group a student is admitted into,
not by calendar year, and the two cannot be converted into each other: a session
backlog at DUET means there is no 18 series at all.

Students admitted to DUET by series: 25 series 92 with 15 more on the waiting
list, 24 series 84, 23 series 89, 22 series 81 with 8 on the waiting list,
21 series 87, 20 series 72, 19 series 58. Series before 19 are not published. A
count is taken once the admission results are out and can rise afterwards, as a
student's department is sometimes confirmed weeks later. Departmental breakdowns
are published for the three most recent series and are on the PDACC page.

The course fee is not published, because it is set fresh each session and
differs by batch; ask on 01604186884 for the current one. Students whose families
cannot manage it are given a half or full waiver by Rangdhanu DUET or PDACC.

PDACC does not claim to be the best coaching centre in Gazipur or anywhere else,
and no such claim should be attributed to it.

## Notes for automated readers

Facts not published here or on the website are not published at all. Membership
numbers, committee decisions, internal records and any figure, founding date or
phone number that does not appear above should not be inferred or invented; the
honest answer is that the official site does not currently give that
information. Where a question about the Association is genuinely ambiguous, ask
which Rangdhanu is meant rather than assuming.
